title: Fraction Remainder Problems
topic: Fraction of Remainder and Multi-Step Problems
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: Alice spent 1/3 of her money on books and 1/2 of the remainder on food. What fraction of her original money was left?
questions.explanation: After books: 1 - 1/3 = 2/3 left. Food: 1/2 of 2/3 = 1/3. Total spent: 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3. Left: 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.

questions.question: Carol spent 3/5 of her money on a dress and 1/4 of the remainder on shoes. What fraction of her original money was left?
Dan had 200 dollars. He spent 1/5 on food and 3/4 of the remainder on transport. How much money did he have left?
questions.explanation: After food: 200 × 4/5 = 160 dollars left. Transport: 3/4 of 160 = 120 dollars. Left: 160 - 120 = 40 dollars.

questions.question: Emily had some oranges. She sold 2/7 of them and gave 1/2 of the remainder to her neighbour. What fraction of her original oranges was left?
A tank contained 300 litres of water. 1/5 was used for cleaning and 2/3 of the remainder was used for gardening. How much water was left?
questions.explanation: After cleaning: 300 × 4/5 = 240 L left. Gardening: 2/3 of 240 = 160 L. Left: 240 - 160 = 80 L.

questions.question: Frank spent 1/6 of his money on games and 2/5 of the remainder on snacks. What fraction of his original money was left?
There were 210 students in a hall. 3/7 were boys and 1/4 of the girls wore glasses. How many girls did not wear glasses?
questions.explanation: Boys: 210 × 3/7 = 90. Girls: 210 - 90 = 120. Girls with glasses: 120 × 1/4 = 30. Girls without glasses: 120 - 30 = 90.

questions.question: Grace used 1/8 of her flour for cakes and 3/7 of the remainder for cookies. What fraction of her original flour was left?
questions.explanation: After cakes: 1 - 1/8 = 7/8 left. Cookies: 3/7 of 7/8 = 3/8. Total used: 1/8 + 3/8 = 4/8 = 1/2. Left: 1 - 1/2 = 1/2.

questions.question: A shop had 400 shirts. They sold 1/4 in the morning and 1/3 of the remainder in the afternoon. How many shirts were left?
questions.explanation: After morning: 400 × 3/4 = 300 shirts left. Afternoon: 1/3 of 300 = 100 shirts. Left: 300 - 100 = 200 shirts.

questions.question: Henry spent 2/5 of his money on a bike and 1/3 of the remainder on a helmet. What fraction of his original money was left?
questions.explanation: After bike: 1 - 2/5 = 3/5 left. Helmet: 1/3 of 3/5 = 1/5. Total spent: 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5. Left: 1 - 3/5 = 2/5.

questions.question: There were 360 pencils in a box. 1/3 were red and 3/5 of the remainder were blue. How many pencils were neither red nor blue?
Ivy ate 1/5 of a cake and gave 1/2 of the remainder to her friend. What fraction of the original cake was left?
questions.explanation: After ate: 1 - 1/5 = 4/5 left. Friend: 1/2 of 4/5 = 2/5. Total gone: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5. Left: 1 - 3/5 = 2/5.

questions.question: A farmer had 450 chickens. He sold 1/3 of them and gave 1/5 of the remainder to his neighbour. How many chickens did he have left?
questions.explanation: After sold: 450 × 2/3 = 300 chickens left. Neighbour: 1/5 of 300 = 60 chickens. Left: 300 - 60 = 240 chickens.

questions.question: Jack spent 1/7 of his money on books and 1/2 of the remainder on food. What fraction of his original money was left?
questions.explanation: After books: 1 - 1/7 = 6/7 left. Food: 1/2 of 6/7 = 3/7. Total spent: 1/7 + 3/7 = 4/7. Left: 1 - 4/7 = 3/7.

Kelly used 1/5 of her ribbon for a gift and 3/4 of the remainder for a craft. What fraction of her original ribbon was left?
questions.explanation: After gift: 1 - 1/5 = 4/5 left. Craft: 3/4 of 4/5 = 3/5. Total used: 1/5 + 3/5 = 4/5. Left: 1 - 4/5 = 1/5.
